source.title: HCD Letter of Technical Assistance to the City of Los Angeles, Table 1 'SB 79 Development Standards' (June 22, 2026)

adjacent.label: Adjacent (within 200 ft of a pedestrian access point)

quarter.label: Within ¼ mile of a TOD stop

half.label: Between ¼ and ½ mile of a TOD stop (cities with ≥35,000 residents)

1.label: Tier 1 — heavy rail or very high frequency commuter rail

2.label: Tier 2 — light rail, high frequency commuter rail, or bus with full-time dedicated lane

provisions.text: A qualifying housing development is an allowed use on any site zoned for residential, mixed, or commercial development in a TOD zone. HCD reads “zoned for” to include any zone that principally or conditionally permits residential, mixed-use, or commercial uses.
provisions.cite: Gov. Code § 65912.157(a); HCD TA letter to Los Angeles (6/22/2026), Q1

provisions.text: Height, density, and residential FAR figures are minimums the city must allow (the city may not impose lower limits). Local zoning that allows more still applies.
provisions.cite: Gov. Code § 65912.157(a); HCD TA letter to Los Angeles, Table 1

provisions.text: The project must include at least 5 dwelling units.
provisions.cite: HCD SB 79 Housing Element Sites guidance

provisions.text: Distance is measured in a straight line from the nearest edge of the parcel to a pedestrian access point of the TOD stop. A parcel only partly inside a zone qualifies in its entirety unless it is subdivided.
provisions.cite: Gov. Code § 65912.157(b); HCD TA letter to Los Angeles, Q2

provisions.text: Adjacency intensifier: projects within 200 ft of a pedestrian access point get +20 ft height, +40 du/ac, and +1.0 residential FAR.

SB 79 does not set numeric setbacks, lot coverage, or open-space requirements. The jurisdiction’s objective development standards apply, but they may not physically preclude the SB 79 density and floor area.
provisions.cite: HCD TA letter to Los Angeles (6/22/2026), Q13; Gov. Code § 65912.160(c)(1)

provisions.text: Projects remain eligible for State Density Bonus Law incentives, concessions, waivers, and parking reductions.

SB 79 projects may not be located on a site with more than two units of rent- or price-controlled housing occupied by tenants in the past 7 years, or where such housing was demolished in the 7 years before the application.
Affordability criteria and labor standards apply.
SB 79 is optional for applicants: a project may instead proceed under local zoning.
provisions.cite: HCD TA letter to Los Angeles, Q3

provisions.text: SB 79 does not apply in unincorporated county areas until the county’s 7th-cycle housing element is due.
